item.title: I Lit Up a TLA+ Model Checker on a Machine That Had No Java
item.description: Claude Code's author claims Opus caught a race condition with TLA+, and the internet is crowing about formal verification. I did the opposite of the hype: on a machine with no root, no desktop, and no preinstalled Java, I manually lit up TLA+'s model checker TLC and wrote my own 40-line lost-update spec. The 2.2MB jar I pulled from GitHub couldn't even recognize textbook stuttering on my box. This post is about exactly how far I actually got, where it broke, and what TLA+ can and can't express — judged against the boundaries I poked at myself.

item.title: On a Two-Core Box, I Cut a Rust Build From 20 Seconds to 0.05
item.description: Nethercote, who leads the rustc team, published on how the compiler got faster and it hit #1 on HN. He measured the inside of the compiler; I measured the user side. On a two-core box with no Rust at all, I brought the toolchain up by hand and ran a build benchmark: 20s cold, 0.05s incremental, a 330x gap. This is what I actually got, the one lever I could not install, and why I cannot reproduce his 4.57%.

item.title: The Go Toolchain Floor: Why ADK Go 2.x Needs 1.26.6+, and the Go 1.26/1.27 Changes That Actually Affect Agent Code
item.description: ADK Go v2.4.0 requires go 1.26.6 in go.mod. This article explains how that enforcement works, the GOTOOLCHAIN traps behind restrictive networks, and the Go 1.26/1.27 changes that genuinely matter for agent code: new(expr), generic methods, Green Tea GC, the goroutineleak profile, the asynctimerchan removal, and the stdversion check.
